title: A derivation extends to adic completions and to localizations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $D:R\to R$ a derivation, i.e. an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$ for all $a,b\in R$. (1) Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/I^n$ the $I$-adic completion and $c:R\to R^\wedge$ the canonical map [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then there is a derivation $D^\wedge:R^\wedge\to R^\wedge$ with $D^\wedge\circ c=c\circ D$ (it is induced by the maps $R/I^{n+1}\to R/I^n$, $a\bmod I^{n+1}\mapsto D(a)\bmod I^n$, well defined since $D(I^{n+1})\subseteq I^n$). (2) Let $W\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset and $\lambda:R\to W^{-1}R$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then there is a unique derivation $D_W:W^{-1}R\to W^{-1}R$ with $D_W\circ\lambda=\lambda\circ D$, namely $D_W(a/w)=D(a)/w-aD(w)/w^2$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PE (lemma-derivation-extends, line 11754), items (1) and (2), and their proof; the last sentence of 07PE (finite type extensions R subset R') is not stated here
